selected.assay: bulk RNA-seq (BGI DNBseq, 100 bp PE), human vastus lateralis; STAR 2.7.3a + RSEM (S4.9.1.p1)
selected.design: parallel-group randomized trial (S2.1.p1, S4.5.p1, S4.6.p1): healthy men allocated to SIE or MICE; RNA-seq on 12 per group (Fig. 1D: n = 12 per group; S4.9.1.p1: 72 samples = 24 participants x 3 timepoints) at rest (pre), early recovery (+3 h from start of exercise) and late recovery (+24 h) (S2.2.p1)
selected.repeated_measure_unit: participant (3 biopsies per participant; participants nested within exercise group)
selected.sample_inclusion: all 72 RNA-seq samples (24 participants x 3 timepoints); no exclusions stated
selected.primary_estimand: within-group exercise response at +3 h and +24 h vs rest, for MICE and SIE separately (S2.2.p2, Fig. 1E), and the between-group difference in exercise response (time x group interaction) at +3 h and +24 h (S2.3.p1)
planned_contrasts: SIE vs MICE difference in response at +3h (S2.3.p1; paper: 207 transcripts, 116 larger up in SIE, 91 larger up in MICE)
SIE vs MICE difference in response at +24h (S2.3.p1; paper: 16 transcripts)
selected.normalization: not stated beyond 'following previously published guidelines' (S4.9.1.p1); 13,295 transcripts detected across samples (S2.2.p1) implies a low-expression filter
selected.paper_method: limma and DESeq2 on RSEM read counts in R (S4.9.1.p1); which package produced which count is not stated; fGSEA for the mitostress gene set

paper_results.ORA: SIE-larger-up genes at 3 h enriched for protein folding / UPR terms (Fig. 2B)
paper_results.GSEA: mitostress set enriched only after SIE (NES 1.50, FDR < 0.01)

decisions.reason: S2.2.p1-p2 and S2.3.p1 give the six contrasts and their counts; S4.9.1.p1 gives the pipeline (STAR/RSEM, limma and DESeq2); S4.10.p1 'For RNA-sequencing and proteomics, an adjusted p value (p < 0.05) was used' with no fold-change rule. Participants were randomized to one group (parallel design, S2.1.p1/S4.5.p1/S4.6.p1), so subjects are nested in group.

checks: 72 samples = 24 participants x 3 timepoints, as in S4.9.1.p1
vastus lateralis, Homo sapiens, BGISEQ-500, STAR/RSEM in data_processing

decisions.reason: The paper deposits RNA-seq under GSE302582 (S4.9.1.p1); the series cites PMID 41326383; the per-sample RSEM genes.results files in GSE302582_RAW.tar cover all 72 GSMs.

Tar columns become GSM ids, matched exactly to the metadata index (72/72). grp and time from the title; time '+2.5h' (GEO) is the paper's '+3 h' biopsy (S2.2.p1 counts from exercise start), recoded h3. Participant numbers restart within each group (Participant #1 exists in both MICE and SIE, each with 3 samples) and the paper is parallel-group, so the subject key is group + participant number (e.g. MICE_1), 24 subjects with 3 samples each.

selected.recommended_method: DESeq2 on rounded expected counts; limma on log2(CPM+1)

decisions.reason: Each GSM file is an RSEM genes.results table (gene_id, transcript_id(s), length, effective_length, expected_count, TPM, FPKM); the merged matrix holds the expected_count column (A1BG 6.00 in GSM9106607 equals expected_count, not TPM 0.25/FPKM 0.14), 91.6% integers with fractional values from multi-mapping, max 1.23e6, library sizes 10.1-15.5 M. data_processing: STAR, RSEM, limma/edgeR. Paper S4.9.1.p1 used 'read counts' from RSEM. Matches the paper's input.

selected.formula: within group: ~ subject + time; between-group response difference: limma on within-subject changes (followup - pre) ~ 0 + grp

decisions.reason: S2.2.p2 reports within-group responses at each recovery time vs rest; S2.3.p1 reports transcripts 'upregulated to a larger extent' in SIE vs MICE, i.e. a difference in the exercise response (time x group interaction), not a cross-sectional group difference. Each cell has 12 participants. Exploratory: h24 vs h3 within each group and SIE vs MICE at each single timepoint (between-subject, cross-sectional).

Each participant contributes pre, +3 h and +24 h biopsies, so participant is a blocking unit for the within-subject time contrasts (DESeq2 ~ subject + time within each group) and is removed by differencing in the interaction (limma on followup - pre per participant). Subjects are nested in group, so a single additive ~ subject + grp:time DESeq2 model is not full rank in the runner; the two routes avoid that aliasing. No batch or other covariate is recorded; none added.

selected.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald) for within-group time contrasts; limma (moderated t) on within-subject log2(CPM+1) changes for the group x time interaction
selected.formula: DESeq2: ~ subject + cell(time) fitted per group; limma paired change: (log2CPM followup - log2CPM pre) ~ 0 + C(grp)

paper_route.method: limma and DESeq2 (R), exact model unstated
paper_route.reason: the paper names both packages without saying which produced which result or the model formula; DESeq2 with subject blocking is used for the within-group responses and limma for the response difference

deviations: RSEM expected counts rounded to integers for DESeq2
low-expression filter CPM >= 1 in >= 12 samples of each fit (one timepoint cell = 12 participants) as an approximation of the paper's unstated filter (13,295 detected transcripts)
interaction estimated with limma on log2(CPM+1) within-subject changes (paired change), not a DESeq2 interaction term

decisions.reason: Estimated counts support DESeq2 after documented rounding and limma on log2(CPM+1). The paper used both packages (S4.9.1.p1). The runner cannot fit the nested-subject DESeq2 interaction model, so the response difference uses limma on per-participant changes, which removes subject effects exactly.
S4.10.p1: 'For RNA-sequencing and proteomics, an adjusted p value (p < 0.05) was used to establish statistical significance'; S2.3.p1 'Adj. p < 0.05'. No fold-change rule.
MICE within-group responses (S2.2.p2), one DESeq2 model with participant blocking on the 36 MICE samples; h24 vs h3 exploratory
SIE within-group responses (S2.2.p2), one DESeq2 model with participant blocking on the 36 SIE samples; h24 vs h3 exploratory

SIE vs MICE difference in the exercise response at +3 h and +24 h (S2.3.p1) with limma, one of the paper's packages; per-participant changes remove subject effects; within-group limma responses as a sensitivity check of the DESeq2 counts
cross-sectional SIE vs MICE at each timepoint (between different people); exploratory, not the paper's response-difference estimand

caveats: the paper's exact model and filter are unstated; counts are expected to differ
the paper's mitostress GSEA set (Quiros 2017) is not available here; Hallmark GSEA is a substitute and not a reproduction

decisions.reason: Planned contrasts all run on the paper's samples and threshold; method details are partially specified by the paper.
